comparator.name: Pedagogical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh review 31 October 2026. Adopted ESSB EER 2026–2027 Appendix III E p44 verifies the complete 17-component 180-EC pathway and first-listed Pedagogiek option. Appendix I D pp32–33 establishes pedagogical and educational inquiry. Articles 3.6,4.1–4.2 establish approved minor choice and progression. Programme and careers pages corroborate current identity and distinguish later qualifications. The exact linked 2025-09 brochure is labelled 2026–2027 and supports its illustrative topics; a separate 2019-10 URL now holds a 2027–2028 edition and does not control credits. No old audit approval inherited.

routeSelection.basis: Generic Pedagogical Sciences target. The two 15-EC final-year options are equally general within their distinct domains; use first-listed Pedagogiek in adopted 2026–2027 EER Appendix III E p.44 as neutral tie-break, not UCR fit.

audience.programmeDescription: Students examine how children develop and learn in families, schools and communities. They combine theories of education and upbringing with developmental psychology, research methods and practice. The Pedagogiek option focuses on pedagogical support.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR combination studies child development, family and peer influences, and youth support. Erasmus develops these subjects through specialist pedagogy, educational design and assessment of families facing difficulties with upbringing.

curriculum.limitation: The pathway includes a 15-EC minor and a compulsory 22.5-EC bachelor project. The final-year pedagogical support option is shown; the alternative education-sciences option is not combined with it.

alternatives.label: Child development, learning and youth support
alternatives.concept: Study how children develop and how families, peers and schools shape their lives. Combine developmental psychology and youth resilience with assessment, quantitative and qualitative research, and communication in a school or community setting.
alternatives.labelReason: Developmental psychology, family and peer influences, youth support and research recur across the six semesters.
progression: Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics and the other psychology and cognition courses that require it. Introductory rhetoric precedes the school-based project. Quantitative and qualitative methods and evidence synthesis support academic study.

trace: Introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of behaviour and mental processes.
Introduces sociological reasoning through classical theories, their historical settings and perspectives that address exclusions from the discipline.
Introduces the molecular and cellular foundations of life and biomedical science.
Introduces the scientific study of how thoughts, feelings and behaviour are shaped by other people and social situations.
Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project.
Studies nervous systems and behaviour from comparative, evolutionary and physiological perspectives.
Develops qualitative inquiry from research design and preparation through data collection, management, analysis and dissemination.
Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research.
Deepens understanding of neuroanatomy, neurophysiology and the experimental study of higher cognitive functions.
Examines health and illness through interactions among biological, psychological and sociocultural factors.
Teaches rhetorical analysis and persuasive communication through classical history, theory and practice.
Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action.
Examines mental health and psychopathology across the lifespan using a biopsychosocial perspective.
Examines physical, cognitive, emotional, social and personality development from prenatal life through old age and death.
Applies rhetoric through community-engaged work with local primary-school children.
Examines youth radicalization and educational prevention through psychology, education, sociology, political science and peace education.
Focuses on civil society through critical, neo-functionalist and decolonial social theory.
Examines contemporary persuasion through communication studies, social psychology and ethical analysis, then applies it in community-engaged work.
Studies normal function and regulation in the adult human body, linking molecular and cellular processes to integrated organ systems.
Introduces clinical psychological assessment and major psychotherapeutic approaches across the lifespan.
Teaches systematic review and meta-analysis for synthesizing evidence in medical, behavioural and related research.
Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language.
Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading.
